page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The configuration includes 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is provided via a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance offers an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several core metrics. The instance achieves a multi-core stress-ng CPU score of 6870.73 and a PassMark CPU score of 7626.07, both placing in the middle tier of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is also moderate, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 382.09 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 40.38 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1304.38 and a weak single-threaded gzip compression rate of 21.98 GB/sec. Large-scale processing tasks like medium-model LLM inference show poor performance, with text generation speeds dropping to 6.2 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r5dn.2xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio combined with local NVMe storage, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive compute capabilities. The inclusion of local SSD storage reduces the need for external storage attachments for temporary data. This profile is suitable for database operations, caching layers like Redis, and memory-intensive data processing tasks that fit within the 64 GB memory footprint.
